coaching.headline: Revenant ate our bottom duo alive all game, and we lost nine structures while taking three.
coaching.team: Revenant finished with 13 kills, nine on Kira and Steel, and the most hero damage in the game. The best stretch for the team was a 4-1 teamfight followed by Fangtooth and two enemy outer towers. Both later teamfights went the enemy's way: the first went 2-4, with an inner tower, Orb Prime and two inhibitors falling after that fight, and the second went 1-3 shortly before the Core fell. The enemy turned six of eight won fights into prizes; the team turned two of five.
coaching.lossReflection: The alternative was to make Revenant the fight. Revenant was killable: Iggy & Scorch got Revenant twice, and Kira and Steel once each. Taking teamfights only when Riktor's Skewer, Countess's Feast or Steel's Shield Slam could reach Revenant first, and letting a tower go when none could, aims to shrink the fights Revenant decided. There is no promise the base holds that way, but it beats feeding the same carry all game.

focus.title: Find their carry before trading
focus.action: When their fed carry drops out of sight, Kira and Steel back off toward the nearest teammate and nobody starts a trade until that carry shows again. Next game, count how many of the enemy carry's kills land on our duo.

22.3.call: Steel dropped first to Greystone, yet the team won the fight 4-1 with two Iggy & Scorch kills. Fangtooth and two enemy outer towers followed, but Kira and Steel died in the skirmish between the tower takes. Take the prize, then reset.

25.5.call: Iggy & Scorch fell first to Greystone; Countess killed Belica and Greystone while Revenant killed Kira, Riktor and Steel. An inner tower fell during it and Orb Prime soon after. Two kills mean nothing while their best damage still stands.

30.6.call: The team took an enemy outer tower in this window, but Steel, Kira and Riktor died for one kill on Aurora, and the Core fell shortly after. With two inhibitors already lost, staying alive to defend outranks any tower.

matchup: Aurora had the most objective damage in the game and killed Riktor twice; Belica killed Riktor three times.
Revenant, the physical crit carry, had the most kills in the game.
build: Flux Matrix brings magical armor against Aurora and makes enemies take more magical damage, suiting Riktor's magical abilities.
Tainted Guard cuts healing and bleeds basic attackers, relevant against Revenant and Belica.
eternal: Knell's shred and armor share depend on repeated hits on the same hero.
Resonant Repair is the draft alternative to Fracture against Aurora's, Belica's and Revenant's lockdown, trading damage for surviving it.
augment: Wanton Warden suits a jungler who took more damage than anyone, but it is recovery after the hit, not protection from burst.
Brutal Chains is the alternative if landing Riplash more often matters more, giving up the sustain.
crest: Saphir's Mantle rewards walking into the fight and staying on heroes, which matches a frontline jungler.
improvement: Riktor ran Elafrost and Spectral Schematics from the winning core, with Flux Matrix and Tainted Guard instead of Gaia Greaves.
Tainted Guard covers physical armor plus anti-heal and Flux Matrix answers Aurora's magic, so the build is a sound keep.
Gaia Greaves trades that anti-heal for movement-based damage; nothing in this match proves a build change.

matchup: Iggy & Scorch killed Belica four times and never died to Belica.
The real threats were physical: Greystone's leap killed Iggy & Scorch twice, and Revenant had the most hero damage.
build: Every slot is magical power with health and no armor, with effects that suit fire zones and turrets.
Greystone's Tainted Bastion adds magical armor and cuts the healing of whoever hits Greystone with magic.
eternal: Aion, Philosopher and Arcane Resonance are an economy setup, and Iggy & Scorch finished with the most gold in the game.
Perfection is the draft alternative to Arcane Resonance, adding ability haste while near full health.
augment: Hold This! rewards landing Molotov on heroes all game, growing permanently stronger with each hit.
Badlands Belch is the alternative if finishing low targets matters more, giving up the stacking Molotov damage.
crest: Epoch's stasis adds no distance, so it pays when teammates can turn on a diver like Greystone or Revenant.
improvement: Greystone and Revenant, both physical, accounted for all three deaths, and nothing in the build adds armor.
With the most gold in the game, the damage build is a sound keep.
If physical divers end fights first, a physical armor item trades damage for surviving the first engage.

matchup: Countess killed Greystone twice and never died to Greystone.
Greystone's Tainted Bastion cuts the healing of whoever hits Greystone with magic, touching Blade Siphon and Feast healing.
build: Noxia suits Countess's ability chains, and Overseer makes Feast hit harder and heal.
Tainted Scepter cuts healing against Narbash, the top healer, and Greystone's regeneration; nothing here adds armor.
eternal: Vesh, Lich and Mind Rot fit a spell-damage Countess.
Tithe of Death is the draft alternative to Lich, giving up lifesteal that Tainted Bastion, Tainted Totem and Tainted Rounds could reduce.
augment: Sanguine Slash pays when Countess catches a lone target and adds nothing extra in a crowded fight.
Shadow Strike is the alternative, trading the isolated-target bonus for faster repositioning.
crest: Tempest suits staying inside a fight, with Blade Siphon also hitting everything around Countess.
improvement: The matchup flag notes no armor, but Countess died only twice, so armor is not proven necessary here.
If Revenant or Greystone start ending fights before Feast lands, physical armor over a damage item trades burst for survival.
As built, it is a sound keep.

matchup: Revenant killed Kira four times, and Aurora, with a root and a stun, killed Kira three times.
Reckoning pulls the target into the Nether Realm with Revenant; Narbash heals, stuns with Thunk and mesmerizes.
build: Tainted Rounds is the right answer to Narbash's healing and Revenant's lifesteal.
Onixian Quiver's Onixia passive works only for melee heroes, and nothing in the build adds defense.
eternal: Vermis, Serration and Breach reward long, uninterrupted shooting on one target.
Sub-Surface is the draft alternative to Breach if surviving brawls matters more than the armor cut.
augment: Bringer Of Mercy cycles Shadow Glide and Dusk faster in long fights.
Siphoning Purge is the alternative if Kira needs sustain, giving up the cooldown cycling.
crest: Pacifier's empowered hit applies to Kira's physical damage, and its dash stacks another escape on Shadow Glide and Blink.
improvement: The clearer adjustment is defense: Revenant and Aurora accounted for seven of Kira's eight deaths.
If Revenant keeps winning meetings, compare a defensive item in place of Onixian Quiver, trading attack speed and extra projectiles for survival.
Onixian Quiver has an Onixia passive that does nothing for a ranged hero.

matchup: Revenant killed Steel five times with physical crit damage.
Narbash, with the most healing, adds a stun and mesmerize; Aurora and Greystone each killed Steel twice.
build: Warden's Faith is the direct answer to Revenant: Steel takes less critical-strike damage.
Xenia's ally shields only help Kira when the duo stays together.
There is no anti-heal here, though the team carried four anti-heal items.
eternal: Krix, Regenerative Tissue and Cannibalism are a plain health stack for a tank support.
Festering Wounds is the draft alternative to Regenerative Tissue, letting stuns cut Revenant's healing, giving up out-of-combat regeneration.
augment: Heavy Metal draws on total armor, so every armor item in this build feeds it.
Bulldozer is the peel-minded alternative, giving up the armor-based damage.
crest: Sanctification's tenacity has a clear purpose against Narbash's stun and mesmerize and Revenant's root.
improvement: Steel built none of the winning core, but Warden's Faith is the piece to keep against Revenant.
Tainted Charm is the swap if Revenant's lifesteal or Narbash's healing starts winning fights, at the cost of Xenia's ally shields.
With four anti-heal items already on the team, the current build is a sound keep.

synergy: Our engage/CC: Riktor Riplash (pull), Riktor Shock Therapy (silence 0.8s), Riktor Skewer (suppress 1.25s), Iggy & Scorch Inferno (knockback), Countess Feast (suppress 0.75s). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
We have sustain (Riktor, Steel) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Our damage is 4/5 magical — predictable; one magic-resist item answers most of it. Mix in a physical threat.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.
